claims.text: Systematic variation of elemental composition governs superconducting behavior in high-entropy alloys outside the well-studied material classes.
Introducing refractory elements such as Mo, Nb, Ta, Ti, and Zr can govern superconducting behavior.
The starting material is a solid solution containing at least five elements at no less than 5 atomic percent each.
The intervention introduces refractory elements while systematically varying elemental composition.
Introducing refractory elements alters the alloy's crystal structure.
Introducing refractory elements alters the alloy's electronic properties.
Changes in crystal structure and electronic properties lead to changes in superconducting behavior.
The modified high-entropy alloy will exhibit superconductivity.
The critical temperature will vary with the specific elemental composition.
The starting material without introduced refractory elements provides the critical-temperature baseline.
The compositional variants must remain solid solutions with at least five elements present at no less than 5 atomic percent each.
An absence of any change in superconducting behavior after refractory-element introduction would falsify the hypothesis.
